title: Add runtime-access guidance to the reader prompt
summary: Add a short rule to crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md. When a change reads data or calls a tool at runtime, the reading must name the role or process that runs it, what its permissions allow, and whether the data is reachable from there. Any limit found goes into acceptance_criteria. The audience is the reader agent and the verifiers who judge its readings.

defaults_applied.how: The criteria check that the reader is told to put the limit into criteria, and the budget test checks that the prompt still loads.
cargo test, clippy, and fmt --check are named in a behavior criterion.
One focused bullet in one prompt file.
The wording is plain and precise for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The guidance goes into the reader prompt file crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, as a bullet in 'Reading the request'.
The reader set has a 2,000-token budget and the prompt is near it (docs/decisions.md says it must not grow much), so the wording must be tight; other lines may be trimmed if needed.
A CHANGELOG.md entry may be added, since earlier prompt changes have been logged there.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md has a bullet under 'Reading the request' saying that when a change reads data or calls a tool at runtime, the reading states (1) which role or process runs it, (2) what that runtime may do under its permissions, and (3) whether the data is reachable from there.
The bullet tells the reader to put any limit it finds (unreachable data, denied tool, missing permission) into acceptance_criteria, so the producer and verifier can check it.

Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: the reader prompt set stays within its 2,000-token budget (check_budget) and all tests pass. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
The rule is concise (one or two lines), written for an outside reader, and no other prompt file, athena.toml or defaults.toml changes. The existing reader.md rules are unchanged.

out_of_scope: Changing the reading schema or its field descriptions
departures: A prompt-only edit is small, but the 2,000-token reader budget may force trimming, so I lowered cost slightly and kept the pass rate near the reference.
